text: hey can u make us a framework/runtime png/jpeg/etc encoder/decoder like something similar to sharp since we dont have node/bun but will want the same capability for upcoming purposes and because a lot of newer image models generate high res images need a good way to resolve this in a format that isnt 30mb of b64 or yeah
resolution: Built @reactjit/image, a Sharp-equivalent codec door, since the repo has no node/bun for runtime image work. New gated 'imageops' ingredient (auto-triggers -Dhas-imageops when a cart imports runtime/image.ts via the metafile gate). framework/image/codec.zig decodes (stb_image), resizes (newly-vendored stb_image_resize2), and encodes PNG/JPEG (stb_image_write) + WebP (libwebp dlopen'd lazily, sqlite3-style so PNG/JPEG carts never load it). The design keeps the heavy raw RGBA entirely inside Zig — carts pass compressed bytes or a base64 string in and get small compressed bytes back, which is the direct fix for the user's '30MB of b64' pain. JS API runtime/image.ts is chainable: image(input).resize(w,h,{fit}).webp({quality}).toBuffer()/.toFile(path)/.metadata()/.raw(). Wired build.zig + v8_ingredients.zig + dependency-registry.json (incl. libwebp dynamic-library entry) + ship.ts label. Verified via cart/image_demo.tsx with ./tools/rjit shot: ALL PASS — 1024KB raw RGBA -> 59.9KB PNG -> 1.7KB JPEG -> 0.6KB WebP, and toFile wrote a valid 128x128 JPEG to disk.
